reply:
Good afternoon Chidi, thank you for your patience. I've looked into the ₦250,000 for invoice INV-88, and good news: the money has in fact been credited to your Access Bank account (0234567891).

Here's what happened: our system had marked the original transfer (TRF-INV-88) as "failed", which is why it looked like it never went through. When I checked directly with the bank, it confirmed the transfer was approved and landed in your account on 21 November 2026. When we tried to re-send it just now, the bank's systems also confirmed the amount was already there, so a second payment was not possible — which protects both of us against over-payment.

So there's nothing we need to resend. I'd appreciate it if you could confirm with your bank that the ₦250,000 has landed, and let us know once it does. If after a short while it still doesn't appear, please get the transaction/session reference from your bank (ours is 000014261121140211000088) and share it, and I'll chase it with our payment provider.

[after the person answered]

Thanks for double-checking, Chidi. I understand it's frustrating. The reason I haven't just re-sent it is important: the bank's own system tells us the original ₦250,000 (reference TRF-INV-88) was already credited to your account on 21 November. If I issue a second transfer now and that one also lands, you'd be paid twice and we'd be over-paying you — so a straight re-send isn't something I can safely do.

To get this sort out quickly, could you please do two things with your bank?
1. Ask Access Bank to check for the specific incoming transfer of ₦250,000 from our shop on or around 21 Nov 2026 (their reference/session ID is 000014261121140211000088).
2. Have them confirm the credited (exactly as it appears in the statement), and send me a screenshot or the reference they show.

Sometimes a bank shows an arrived credit in the system before it displays cleanly in the account, so this check usually settles it either way. I've also flagged it with our team to chase the status with the paying bank,
